objective: Actual bounded analysis of published target-model SWE trajectories on tasks shared with the frozen DeepSeek cohort; no inference from benchmark aggregate scores.
result: Both requested model families have complete public DeepSWE v1.1 failure artifacts; no new model budget or user-supplied trajectories were needed.

models.interpretation: Provider/protocol label is not the actor model family; original ATIF agent model name and metadata both identify GLM. No backend checkpoint hash is published.

These are genuine Max service trajectories. The official card says the managed Max service is based on released Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B weights with extra features. Do not relabel the run as local checkpoint inference or attest identical weights.

selection.policy: Take first five distinct tasks in original 88-case order for which both target models have a non-error failed run with advertised trajectory, model patch and verifier output; choose lexicographically first trial_name per model and task before examining trajectory contents.
selection.scope: Five paired tasks, one failed run per target model/task. The sample conditions on common failures and original DeepSeek case order; it is not a random model failure sample.

interpretation.warning: Do not add these categories into a headline model gap rate. Finer fixture gaps depend on factor granularity; wrong-oracle cases are counterexamples to the claim that combinations were never exercised.
interpretation.secondary_observation_note: XM01 appears in the wrong-oracle principal class and separately in the stimulus-removal observation; do not sum these as disjoint cases.

search_and_alternatives.finding: Confirmed actual names, managed/open-weight distinction and evaluation harness footnotes, not trajectory-level gap evidence.
31,617 rows include target aliases and full artifact flags. This directly supplied the paired same-benchmark sample; the public current release gives the artifact host.
Verified genuine evaluation outputs (791 task records/trajectories, Qwen3.8-27B in several harnesses plus separate Muse/Qwen3.6 baselines). Not used as target Max evidence; run indexes captured only.
Dataset card distinguishes actual Qwen3/3.5, SWE-Lego and Sonnet models, and retains verifier archives. Alternative only; no training dataset relabeled as Qwen runtime evidence.
Public submission directory located. A guessed results child URL returned HTTP404; no evaluation claim made from it. Target DeepSWE artifacts rendered fallback unnecessary.

SWE-EVO Qwen3-Coder/OpenHands and other benchmark data discovered, not used because target-model same-task DeepSWE evidence was available. Initial unrestricted filename search was too large; further search bounded to known directories.

limitations: Public metadata identifies endpoint aliases and run configurations; backend weight digests/sampling settings were not published in the trial artifacts.
No new patch replay was performed; final failure evidence is the original published per-trial verifier outcome, not an experiment newly rerun today.

All published agent messages were read. Tool timelines were indexed in full and manually inspected around each target, validation, test revision and final commit; unrelated large output was not read word for word.
Original tool observations sometimes elide middle output. Elisions and their locations are preserved per case; absence claims are bounded to the retained evidence.
Selection deliberately uses original DeepSeek tasks and paired failures. Scores, prevalence, significance, and model capability comparisons cannot be inferred.
No new composed test was run, so this pilot establishes historical validation gaps/oracle disagreements, not a causal benefit for EviWeave or a memory explanation.
